sources.entry: Appsmith - Build admin panels, CRUD apps and workflows. Build everything you need, 10x faster. (Source Code) Apache-2.0 Java/Docker/K8S
Appsmith | Build internal tools, admin panels and dashboards with a low-code UI

summary.one_liner: Appsmith is an open-source low-code platform for building internal tools, admin panels, dashboards, CRUD apps and workflows.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Appsmith as an open-source low-code platform for building custom applications such as dashboards, admin panels, customer 360 views, IT automation and service management tools. It covers development, deployment and maintenance of these apps. Installation is offered as Appsmith Cloud signup or self-hosting via Docker (recommended), Kubernetes, or an AWS AMI, with other options in the installation guides. The README points to a local dev setup guide for building and running Appsmith from source. It also mentions an Appsmith Agents agentic AI platform that connects AI models to private data, though this is described at a high level only. Learning resources (docs, tutorials, videos, templates), Discord, a community portal and support email are listed.
how_to_run: Install with Docker (recommended); see the Docker installation guide
Alternatively deploy on Kubernetes; see the Kubernetes guide
Or use the AWS AMI installation guide
For local development, follow the 'Setup for local development' guide in the docs
Or sign up for Appsmith Cloud instead of self-hosting
notable: Open-source low-code platform under Apache License 2.0
Self-hostable via Docker, Kubernetes, or AWS AMI
Offers a hosted Appsmith Cloud option as an alternative to self-hosting
Includes an Appsmith Agents AI platform for querying private data and configuring automations
caveats: README gives few technical details on architecture, supported databases or integrations
Local development setup is delegated to external documentation
Appsmith Agents is described only at a marketing level
